name: Tamagotchi
blurb: Bandai's 1996 egg-shaped digital pet you fed, cleaned and tried to keep alive
title: Tamagotchi: When It Came Out, How It Worked and Is It Still Sold?
description: Tamagotchi is Bandai's egg-shaped virtual pet, launched in Japan in 1996 for 1,980 yen. It is still made today and passed 100 million units shipped in 2025.
answer: A Tamagotchi is a keychain-sized, egg-shaped digital pet made by Bandai: a tiny pixel creature lives on its screen, and you use three buttons to feed it, play with it, clean up after it and give it medicine, or it gets sick and dies. It launched in Japan on November 23, 1996 for 1,980 yen and in the US on May 1, 1997, and became a worldwide craze. Unlike most 1990s fads it never went away: Bandai still releases new models and reported 100 million units shipped as of July 31, 2025.

body: The original is a plastic egg with a small monochrome screen and three buttons. The story is that an alien creature laid an egg on Earth; it hatches and grows through life stages, and what it becomes depends on how well you look after it.

ul: Meters show hunger and happiness; you feed it meals or snacks and play a simple game
It leaves droppings on screen that you have to flush away
Neglect makes it sick, and medicine cures it
Poor care kills it: Japanese versions show a ghost and gravestone, English versions an angel

body: Bandai says the name combines the Japanese tamago (egg) with the English watch. The idea came from Akihiro Yokoi of WiZ and Aki Maita of Bandai, who shared a 1997 Ig Nobel Prize for it.

What happened

US launch on May 1; 10 million sold by July
Nearly 40 million sold by spring, about half in Japan; the craze cools
20th anniversary reissue of the original in Japan, abroad in 2018
Tamagotchi Uni, the first with Wi-Fi, in a smartwatch shape

body: The first pets could die in less than half a day without care, so children brought them to class and fed them under the desk. They beeped for attention, teachers complained, and many schools banned them. In China the toy was known as 电子鸡 ("electronic chicken"), and many of the ones children carried there were cheap look-alikes rather than Bandai originals.

Yes. Tamagotchi is an active brand: Bandai keeps releasing new models alongside reissues of the 1990s originals, and global sales doubled between 2022 and 2023 as adults who grew up with it and new young players bought in. Bandai has also opened dedicated Tamagotchi shops, including a permanent one in Tokyo.

faq.q: When did the Tamagotchi come out?
faq.a: November 23, 1996 in Japan and May 1, 1997 in the United States.

faq.q: How many Tamagotchis have been sold?
faq.a: Bandai reported 100 million units shipped worldwide as of July 31, 2025.
Bandai explains it as tamago, Japanese for egg, combined with watch: an "egg watch".
